messages.content: I have two Cleveland-area restaurant visits Thursday, May 14. The first is at 8:30 a.m. in Beachwood and the second is in Westlake. That one should wrap around 5:00. Compare flying Wednesday evening with driving from Chicago Wednesday afternoon. I need one hotel night either way, and do not book anything yet.
What are the restaurant addresses, and what time could you leave Chicago Wednesday? Also, if you fly, will you need a rental car or would rides be acceptable?

Beachwood is 26300 Cedar Road. Westlake is  Crocker Park area, 189 Main Street. I can leave home by 2:00 p.m. Wednesday. Use a rental car for the flight option because I may need to carry materials between visits.
I’ll compare door-to-door timing and full estimated costs. For Thursday evening, should I evaluate the earliest practical flight or preserve extra margin after the 5:00 p.m. finish?
Show me the earliest practical flight, but tell me plainly if it is too tight. I cannot leave the Westlake visit before 5:00.

The strongest flight option is United nonstop from ORD Wednesday at 6:15 p.m., arriving CLE at 8:37 p.m. Economy is $286 round trip. Allowing 55 minutes from home to ORD, 90 minutes before departure, and about 40 minutes at CLE for the rental pickup, you would reach a Beachwood hotel around 9:45-10:00 p.m.

The best-positioned hotel is Aloft Cleveland Beachwood, about 8 minutes from the first restaurant and 28-40 minutes from Westlake outside a major incident. One king is $174 including taxes, with free parking. A compact rental from Hertz is $104 including taxes; estimated fuel is $14. The flight plan totals about $578.

Driving at 2:00 p.m. should take roughly 6 hours 15 minutes plus a 30-minute stop, putting you at the hotel around 9:45 p.m. Eastern. Estimated round-trip fuel is $96, tolls $42, and the same hotel is $174, for $312 total. That excludes wear and mileage value.
What is the Thursday return flight, and how much actual margin does it leave? Include rental return and security, not just drive time.

The available nonstop is United CLE-ORD at 7:18 p.m., arriving at 7:49 p.m. Central. From 189 Main Street, the normal drive to the rental facility is 18-25 minutes. If you leave at 5:00, a realistic sequence is rental-fuel stop by 5:15, rental return around 5:35-5:45, shuttle and terminal entry around 5:55-6:05, then security. That leaves about 38-48 minutes before a typical 6:43 boarding cutoff and 73-83 minutes before departure.

It is workable with an on-time 5:00 departure, but not comfortably protected. A 20-minute meeting overrun or heavy traffic would reduce the buffer sharply. The next nonstop is Friday morning, so this is the only same-evening nonstop in the comparison.
Could rides instead of the rental improve that? I still need the materials moved, but they fit in two medium boxes.

Rides would simplify the airport handoff but introduce pickup uncertainty. Estimated trips are CLE to Beachwood $42-$55, hotel to the first restaurant $12-$17, Beachwood to Westlake $46-$62, and Westlake to CLE $28-$38, or $128-$172 total before tips. That makes the flight plan about $588-$632.

If a car is waiting at 5:00 p.m., you could reach the terminal around 5:25-5:35 and retain roughly 68-78 minutes before boarding closes. Prearranging the return ride would help, but two boxes make the rental more dependable throughout the day. The rental option is also similar or lower in cost.
Then keep the rental in the comparison. Is Beachwood still the right hotel if I drive? It seems like I would be going farther east Wednesday and then back west after the second visit.

Yes. Beachwood adds roughly 20-25 minutes Wednesday compared with stopping near Westlake, but it protects the fixed 8:30 a.m. visit. Staying in Westlake would require a 35-50 minute eastbound drive Thursday morning, with more exposure to congestion. From the Beachwood hotel, leaving at 7:55 a.m. gives about 25 minutes of local margin before the first visit.

After that visit, allow 35-45 minutes to Westlake. When the second visit ends, you are already on the west side for the drive toward Chicago, so the hotel’s location does not add mileage to Thursday evening’s trip home.
Lay out the practical schedule and total cost for each option so I can decide later. Include what Thursday night looks like if I drive all the way home.

Flight option: leave home Wednesday at 3:50 p.m.; arrive ORD about 4:45; United departs 6:15 and reaches CLE at 8:37 p.m.; collect the Hertz car and reach Aloft Beachwood around 9:45-10:00. Thursday, leave the hotel at 7:55 a.m.; Beachwood visit at 8:30; allow 35-45 minutes between restaurants; finish Westlake at 5:00; refuel and return the car by about 5:40; reach the terminal around 6:00; depart CLE at 7:18 and arrive ORD at 7:49 Central; reach home about 9:15-9:45 p.m. Estimated total is $578: flight $286, hotel $174, rental $104, fuel $14. The return works, but the margin is vulnerable to any meaningful overrun.

Drive option: leave home Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. Central; take one 30-minute stop; arrive Aloft Beachwood around 9:45 p.m. Eastern. Thursday’s restaurant schedule is the same. Depart Westlake at 5:00 p.m. Eastern, allow about 6 hours 10 minutes of driving plus a 30-minute stop, and reach home around 10:40 p.m. Central. Estimated total is $312: hotel $174, fuel $96, and tolls $42.

Driving saves about $266 and avoids the tight airport transition, but puts roughly 12.5 hours behind the wheel across two days. The flight saves several hours of driving and gets you home about an hour earlier if everything stays on schedule. Nothing has been purchased or held.
